manifest.name: @npmc_5/dsh-neverdie
manifest.description: Automatically revives sessions whose turn was cut short by a DSH process exit or restart, resuming the killed work after restart

bundle.text:
# neverdie bundle patch.
#
# Inserts the single Host plugin row. All knobs live in the plugin's own
# Config schema; see README.md for the full reference.
- insert:
    - id: neverdie
      name: '@npmc_5/dsh-neverdie'
      config: {}

readme.text: [](https://github.com/pinion05/dsh-neverdie) [](./LICENSE)

**Automatically revives DeepSeek Harness (DSH) sessions whose turn was killed by a process exit.** When the host dies mid-turn, every session that was working ends up frozen behind a *"Task stopped — The DSH process exited before this turn finished…"* banner, dead until a human types something. Neverdie removes the human from that loop: after DSH restarts, the killed sessions come back to life on their own and keep working — and their active goals get re-armed so autonomous goal rounds continue.
A DSH process that is killed, crashes, or times out during shutdown takes every running session down with it, and the cut-short turn shows up two different ways depending on how the process went:

- **Hard crash** (SIGKILL, OOM) — the log ends inside an open turn; restart recovery synthesizes a `turn/end` closer with reason `interrupted`.
- **Graceful exit / restart** — the dying process gets to close the running turn itself, as reason `aborted` with cause `disposed`; the aborted tool call leaves an *"Error: tool call aborted"* message as the visible tail of the conversation.

Either way the session sits idle, dead until a human types something — even though the durable session log, the workspace, and the model context are all intact. All the work was *interrupted*, not lost. Long-running jobs (overnight builds, multi-hour agent tasks, goal-driven rounds) deserved better than "click Send again in the morning".

Neverdie is a host-side Cordis plugin that scans once after every boot, finds exactly the sessions that were mid-turn when the previous process died, and re-prompts them with a short configurable message so the agent resumes where it stopped.

- **Precise corpse detection** — a session is revived only when the tail of its balanced log is a `turn/end` closed `interrupted` (hard crash) or `aborted` with cause `disposed` (graceful exit / restart). Deliberate stops (`aborted` cause `user`/`parent`/`hook`), sessions that ended normally, and sessions that already have newer input are never touched — matching on the abort *cause* rather than the visible "Error: tool call aborted" text is what keeps user-stopped sessions dead
- **Survives restart bookkeeping** — the tail walker skips generation markers (e.g. `session/end-seed`) that DSH appends after a restart, and synthesizes the interrupted closers in memory for cold logs, so detection works whether or not the session was reopened first
- **Live-but-idle counts as dead** — the reconnecting web client resumes a session's log without resuming its work; neverdie treats that idle state as a corpse too
- **Goal re-arm** — goal activation is process-local, so the restart that killed the turn also disarmed the session's goal. Neverdie re-arms *active* goals through the supported `goals.resume` path, so automatic continuation rounds keep running. Paused, blocked, complete, or round-ex

1. The host process dies mid-turn. The plugin dies with it — nothing can act at the moment of death.
2. Whatever supervises DSH (e.g. systemd `Restart=on-failure`) starts a new process; the plugin arms and waits `delaySeconds` for boot to settle.
3. One scan: list sessions cheaply, then fully read the balanced log of each fresh, non-archived, root candidate.
4. A backward walker finds the log's last turn end; only an `interrupted` one or an `aborted`-with-`disposed`-cause one, with no newer turn, message, or pending inbox input, qualifies.
5. For each corpse: `resolveAgent` (resumes the cold session), re-arm its active goal if disarmed, queue the revive message, flush to durable storage.
6. The agent continues the interrupted task. If the host dies again, the next boot repeats the cycle within the revive budget.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch |
| `delaySeconds` | `number` | `10` | Wait after host start before the startup scan (0–600) |
| `maxAgeMinutes` | `number` | `60` | Only revive sessions whose interrupted turn is younger than this (1–1440) |
| `maxRevives` | `number` | `5` | Max consecutive neverdie revives per session without genuine user input (0–10) |
| `reviveMessage` | `string` | *(see below)* | The message injected to revive a session |
| `resumeGoals` | `boolean` | `true` | Re-arm active-but-disarmed goals during revival |

Default revive message:

> `[neverdie] The DSH process exited before the previous turn could finish, so that turn was closed. Continue the interrupted task from where it stopped. Tool calls that were cut off have unknown outcomes — inspect their effects before retrying them.`

- **Restart must come from outside.** Neverdie revives sessions *after* the host is back; it cannot restart the host itself. Pair it with a supervisor such as systemd (`Restart=on-failure`).
- **A literal empty prompt is not possible.** The harness rejects whitespace-only prompt content, so revival sends a real (short, configurable) message instead.
- **Root conversations only.** Subagent children are left to their parent sessions, which the parent's own revival reconciles.
- **Freshness bounded.** Corpses older than `maxAgeMinutes` stay dead — raise the window if your host can be down for a long time.
